summary: Split remittance and GL coding mismatch caused by multi-currency rounding during PR->PO invoice auto-match
description:
Issue summary: Several vendor payments for a European supplier were split into two remittance transactions and reconciled to different GL accounts. Impact: GL imbalance and vendor statement mismatch requiring manual intervention to reconcile. Occurs only for invoices auto-matched to POs where invoice currency differs from company base and the system performs a PR-to-PO three-way match with automated rounding adjustments.

Detailed: When invoices issued in EUR are auto-matched against GBP POs and the AP automation performs currency conversion + rounding at line-level, the final payable amount occasionally differs by a fraction of a cent compared to the remittance batching threshold logic. The remittance engine treats the residual micro-amount as a separate remittance line causing: (1) two outgoing payment remittances, (2) one remittance posted to the correct vendor account/GL but the residual line posted to the suspense GL (7010), and (3) vendor statement showing an unapplied credit.

Expected behavior: Single remittance per vendor invoice where amounts convert and round consistently; GL postings should use the invoice's mapped cost center/GL mapping.

Actual behavior: Split remittances and partial posting to suspense GL, causing AP run exceptions and manual recon required.
impact: ~12 vendor payments affected across the last AP cycle; accounting reported a £3.46 net suspense balance that prevented automated month-end close for the EU legal entity. Risk: manual payouts and incorrect GL balances if not remediated before month close.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create PO in GBP with line items totaling GBP 14,523.47
2) Supplier submits invoice in EUR equivalent with line-level amounts that when converted produce micro-rounding differences (example invoice total EUR 17,345.12),
3) Run the AP auto-match job (three-way match) in prod eu-west test slice
- Observe currency conversion applied per line using daily FX rate feed
4) Execute payment batch generation for the normal run with remittance threshold logic enabled (remit_split_threshold=0.01),
5) Observe payment batch output and GL postings: two remittance entries generated for same invoice and one line posted to suspense GL 7010.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Finance (Maya) flagged multiple vendor statement mismatches on 2026-03-09 and escalated to helpdesk.
Checked FX feed: No gaps; daily rate used 2026-03-08 EUR->GBP 0.83729 (confirmed in rates-service logs).
AP matching logs: Line-level rounding applied after conversion; one line retained 0.005 GBP which is rounded down and treated as an orphan residual by remittance engine.

Remittance engine: current implementation splits payment when post-conversion residual > remit_split_threshold. Threshold default is 0.01 but due to floating point precision the residual evaluated to 0.010000000000009 which triggered split.
GL mapping: Orphan residual is assigned to suspense GL 7010 by remittance pipeline; mapping rule doesn't consider sub-cent reconciliation bucket when invoice has cost-center override.
Related logs: payments-service batch 2026-03-09-AP-4189 shows two payment rows for vendor CHF-INV-11234; see payments log ids PAY-20260309-7781 and PAY-20260309-7782.
logs: gl-posting: txn=GL-90011 credit=14523.47 debit=14523.46 suspense_post=0.01 account=7010
root_cause: Floating point precision and line-level rounding interacting with remittance split threshold logic; remittance engine comparison uses decimal floats instead of normalized fixed-point, causing rare >threshold evaluation and split behavior.
workaround: Finance can run the ‘consolidate-residuals’ admin job to merge small residuals into the main remittance for the affected vendor IDs; manual journal entry posted to clear suspense GL 7010 for the interim month-close. Prefer not to change thresholds mid-cycle.
resolution_plan: 1) Patch remittance engine to use normalized decimal (pennies) arithmetic and clamp residuals < 0.05 GBP to main remittance unless vendor override present (PR target: payments-service v2.14). 2) Add pre-flight validation to AP matching to surface residuals > 0.005 GBP in the dashboard. 3) Backfill affected GL entries and run consolidate-residuals for impacted batches. 4) Release hotfix to production after code review and QA in staging (eu-west test slice).
